solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Studies a quiet run on credit

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it, so the credit abbreviation comes first

parts.note: CR is the standard abbreviation for credit in accounts
SH is the call for silence
a course is a run, as in the course or run of events

explanation.surface: Someone takes a quiet jog and pays for it on the card.
explanation.definitionFit: An intensive short programme of learning is a set of studies packed into little time.

clue.text: Ride around working for twister

indicators.note: the bike-riding word goes round the outside of the word for working

parts.note: to cycle is to ride a bike
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A bike ride is taken round on the job, in search of a tornado.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is an informal name for a violent rotating storm, here the tropical kind.

clue.text: Marry an ecologist, giving up name

parts.note: the indefinite article written as its single-letter form

indicators.note: the phrase gives up, or loses, one letter from the ecologist phrase

parts.note: a Green is an environmental campaigner

explanation.surface: Wedding an environmentalist means surrendering one's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: To marry two accounts is to make them tally or correspond, the same as being in accord.

clue.text: In short, a revolutionary must welcome independent academic

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in, or welcome, a letter in their midst
the letters of the words before it are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: Put briefly, any rebel has to embrace someone who stands apart from parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short' looks like 'briefly' but is anagram fodder: IN SHORT A reworked by 'revolutionary' gives HISTORAN, and 'must welcome' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar of the past is a kind of academic, studying and teaching events gone by.

clue.text: Blades or Owls against Reading, surprisingly taking the leaders

indicators.note: only the leading letter of each of the four words is used

explanation.surface: Sheffield United or Sheffield Wednesday play Reading and an upset follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blades and the Owls are nicknames of Sheffield's two football clubs, and Reading is another English club; here Blades is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat ends of rowing implements are called blades, and rowers call the whole implement a blade.

clue.text: Given compensation, considered taking in wife for good

indicators.note: the word for considered takes in a new letter in place of an old one
the letter for wife stands in for the letter for good

parts.note: to have regarded something is to have considered it
G is the abbreviation for good
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A man is paid after a thoughtful decision to take a wife for good.
explanation.definitionFit: To be paid back or recompensed for effort is to be given compensation for it.

clue.text: Old fool — one whose time is over

parts.note: ex- means former or old
to con someone is to fool them

explanation.surface: An elderly simpleton has run out of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' is the prison sentence: a former inmate has done his time.
explanation.definitionFit: A former prisoner has served his sentence, so his stretch inside is finished.

clue.text: Signal left on board and stop

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship, as seen by someone aboard facing forward
to end is to stop

explanation.surface: Someone flashes a message from the left side of a ship and halts.
explanation.definitionFit: To portend is to foreshadow or be a sign of something to come, so to signal it.

clue.text: Penchant for separation, perhaps, in final performance

definitions.meaning: split the word as pen chant: a pen is a female swan and a chant is a song
a last appearance or work before retirement

explanation.surface: A liking for splitting up shows in someone's farewell show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penchant' looks like a liking, but 'for separation' asks you to split it into PEN (female swan) and CHANT (song).
explanation.definitionFit: The legend that swans sing only as they die gave the name to a last appearance or work.

clue.text: Opener from county second team?

parts.note: Cork is a county of Ireland
a crew is a team, as of rowers

explanation.surface: A county's reserve side is asked who will open the batting.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle opener with a spiral spike pulls corks out of wine bottles.

clue.text: Shrink from cold, getting more depressed with no hat

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: the word loses its top or first letter, as a head loses its hat

parts.note: lower means more depressed, sunk further down

explanation.surface: Someone recoils from the chill, more downcast for having no hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To cringe or recoil in fear is to shrink away from something.

clue.text: Son rejected by new coolest cat

indicators.note: the letters are made new by being rearranged
the letter for son is thrown out of the reworked letters

explanation.surface: A boy is spurned by the trendiest new feline.
explanation.walkthrough: COOLEST without S leaves COOLET, which 'new' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a wild spotted cat of the Americas.

clue.text: Soldiers needing jig, say, to secure new heavy weaponry

parts.note: OR stands for Other Ranks, soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: the dance word holds, or secures, the letter for new inside it

parts.note: a jig is one example of a dance

explanation.surface: Troops who want a jig must get hold of fresh big guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery and military supplies such as big guns are known collectively by this word.

clue.text: Extract allowable by right of licence

indicators.note: one piece stands beside the other
the right-hand end of the word, its last letter, is taken

parts.note: licit means lawful or allowable

explanation.surface: Someone extracts what is allowed by holding a right under licence.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit a response is to draw it out, which is to extract it.

clue.text: The compiler's on phone, getting static

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself: the compiler is gives I'M
a mobile is a mobile phone

explanation.surface: The setter is on the phone but getting interference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Static' tempts as crackle on the line; it means not moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Something static stays still and cannot move.

clue.text: Useless personnel from a musical stage, in parts?

definitions.meaning: staff who add nothing to an organisation

definitions.text: from a musical stage, in parts?
definitions.meaning: The ... Stage is a song from the musical Calamity Jane, so the word is part of that stagecoach's name

explanation.surface: Dud staff come from a stage show in sections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' looks theatrical, but it is the stagecoach of the song 'The Deadwood Stage' from Calamity Jane.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead branches are useless, so the term covers staff who contribute nothing.

clue.text: Eccentric initiated as expert in nutrition

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: An oddball is admitted to the society as a food specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet professional advises people on what to eat, so is a specialist in nutrition.

clue.text: Turning into the wind across river, and following

indicators.note: the sailing word lies across, or around, the letter for river

parts.note: tacking is a sailing manoeuvre that turns the bow through the wind

explanation.surface: A yacht heads into the breeze across a river, pursuing something.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracking someone is following their trail.

clue.text: Classes of marine trained on board ship

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go on board, inside the ship abbreviation

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: training reshapes something, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A marine receives instruction aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Seminars are small teaching classes, typically at a college or university.

clue.text: South American volunteers with popular support

parts.note: US is short for United States, so American
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A Southern American's volunteers have broad public backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain something is to support or keep it going.

clue.text: Agree to differ on millions being inadequate

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece on another comes after it

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million or millions

indicators.note: the letters are made to differ from their order

explanation.surface: Two parties agree to disagree over sums of money that are not enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agree to differ' reads as a set phrase, but 'to differ' rearranges AGREE into EAGRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A meagre portion is scant, too little to be enough.

clue.text: Line dismissed by travelling salesmen as a group

indicators.note: the letters move about, being travelling salesmen in the surface
the letter for line is sent away from the salesmen

explanation.surface: Commercial travellers all line up together and are sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: SALESMEN without L leaves SASEMEN, which 'travelling' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: This French borrowing means all together, everyone as a body.

clue.text: Take away some land on reserve

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece on another follows it

parts.note: a sub is a substitute or reserve player
a tract is an area of land

explanation.surface: A plot of land on a nature reserve is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To subtract is to take one number away from another.

clue.text: Extract from legislature's inquiry

indicators.note: the letters are taken from inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A passage is quoted from a parliamentary investigation.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is a sticky substance extracted from trees such as pines.

clue.text: Pronouncement from investigators turning stomach

indicators.note: the investigators' abbreviation is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
tum is an informal word for stomach

explanation.surface: Detectives make a statement that makes your stomach turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictum is an authoritative statement, a formal pronouncement.

clue.text: Cheers supporting article and letter from abroad

indicators.note: in a down clue, the supporting piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: the is the definite article
ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: Thanks for backing the item and a note sent from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter from abroad' suggests post; it is a character of a foreign alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, so a letter from a foreign script.

clue.text: Gun supplied by company officer

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: A firearm is issued by a company commander.
explanation.definitionFit: Colt is a famous make of revolver, so a gun.

clue.text: Finally losing tail in the hills of Africa

indicators.note: the last letter of the phrase is dropped, as an animal might lose its tail

parts.note: at last means finally

explanation.surface: An animal finally loses its tail up in the African hills.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlas Mountains run across north-west Africa.

clue.text: Admirers left one covered by dodgy dossier

indicators.note: the two letters are wrapped inside the reworked letters
dodgy means suspect or unsound, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Fans quit when one is exposed in a suspect file.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolisers worship someone, so they are devoted admirers.

clue.text: Singer's evening at home bit of a blow

parts.note: night is evening time
in means at home
a blow is a gust or storm of wind, and a gale is a strong one

explanation.surface: A singer spends the evening indoors while a storm blows.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightingale is a songbird famous for singing at night.
